title: Graph Beta: replay graph revision events into state
description: Production prerequisite for task-dd4ffa0c40834c59892f957fbf61fb23. Measurement at HEAD a42ae2f: @moe/core exports reduceGraphRevision for commands and emits GraphRevisionEvent, but has no public event apply/replay/hydration function. A durable projection cannot rebuild authority from events without reimplementing the lifecycle. Land the core-owned event replay surface that validates exact event shapes/order/version/identity and reconstructs GraphRevisionState. Not in scope: snapshot content, persistence, daemon transport, runtime-kind wiring, or authoritative design edits.
definitionOfDone: A public @moe/core production replay function folds readonly unknown event input into the exact immutable GraphRevisionState represented by GraphRevisionEvent, using the same lifecycle/version/identity invariants as reduceGraphRevision.

Created/submitted/approved/activated/rejected/superseded sequences reconstruct every state field and accept duplicate delivery only under the explicitly defined idempotent identity; missing create, gaps/reordering, impossible transitions, conflicting duplicate bytes, bad bindings/epochs, extra keys, or hostile objects fail closed.
Every refusal returns an exact stable core code and CORE graph-revision layer; UNKNOWN/corrupt history never yields partial state or graph authority.

Focused generated lifecycle/permutation/hostile-input tests assert exact code/layer, prove nonzero cases, compare replayed state/events against the public reduceGraphRevision production surface, and include ACTIVE and SUPERSEDED accepted controls.
The @moe/core root exports the replay symbols with LF bridge/loadability coverage, and completion names task-dd4ffa0c40834c59892f957fbf61fb23 as the real consumer.
taskRails: Do not create a daemon-side parallel lifecycle reducer; event hydration belongs beside reduceGraphRevision in @moe/core.
Snapshot hostile input before inspection and preserve stable reason code/layer distinctions for order, version, identity, binding, and shape failures.
Use TDD, <=250 lines per production file and split before 400, nonzero generated counts, mutation drill against the production replay surface, and explicit-path commit only.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED — write `graph-revision-replay.test.ts` against the new public `replayGraphRevisionEvents(unknown)` surface. Generate every legal lifecycle path by driving the real `reduceGraphRevision` production function, collect its emitted events, replay them, and assert byte/value-equal frozen state for DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, ACTIVE, REJECTED from each legal source, and SUPERSEDED (including initial versus succession activation). Assert the generated transition/path count is nonzero and covers every member of `GRAPH_REVISION_COMMAND_KINDS`/event-kind vocabulary. Add exact code+layer cases for non-array/sparse/extra-keyed/hostile input, empty/missing or repeated create, malformed event/witness/binding, version gap/regression/reordering, impossible lifecycle, mismatched goal/hash/expectedGoalVersion, invalid activation/succession epoch, events after terminal state, exact duplicate delivery, and conflicting duplicate bytes.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED established. `npx vitest run --root . packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-replay.test.ts` fails with `Error: Cannot find module './graph-revision-replay.js'` — red for the absence of the production module, not for a broken fixture. No implementation exists yet.

GENERATION IS REAL, NOT HAND-WRITTEN. Every legal history is produced by driving the actual `reduceGraphRevision` through a `Step` list and collecting the events it emitted; `drive()` THROWS on a rejected fixture command rather than returning a short history, because a path that stopped early would still replay cleanly and prove nothing about the lifecycle it claims. Refusal fixtures are then one deliberate drift from a generated history (`mutatedLast`), so both operands are never hand-authored — that is the tautology this suite has to avoid, since replay's only honest oracle is the reducer that owns the lifecycle.

11 legal paths cover all six lifecycles: DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, ACTIVE (compound from PENDING_APPROVAL AND separate from APPROVED AND as a named successor), REJECTED (from DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL and APPROVED), SUPERSEDED (after both activation shapes). ACTIVE and SUPERSEDED accepted controls are separate named tests per DoD 4, asserting the rebuilt `graphEpoch` (1 initial, 2 for a successor) and the exact five-key `boundHashes` identity.

NONZERO/COVERAGE GUARD (rail: a sweep producing zero cases passes while testing nothing): one test asserts `LEGAL_PATHS.length > 0` and that the driven command kinds equal `GRAPH_REVISION_COMMAND_KINDS` exactly, the driven event kinds equal `GRAPH_REVISION_EVENT_KINDS` exactly, and the reached lifecycles equal all six. A separate test asserts every published member of `GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_CODES` is actually exercised by the refusal table — an unreachable published code is an unverifiable refusal.

REFUSAL TABLE: 38 cases, each asserting code AND layer together as one string (`${layer}/${code}`) so a sibling layer answering first cannot read as this refusal. Covers non-array/string/null/undefined/sparse/extra-own-key/getter-entry histories, cyclic + exotic-prototype + symbol-keyed events, empty history, missing create, duplicate create, create at version != 1, unknown kind, missing/extra event keys, non-hex hashes, empty refs, truth-floor violations on submission and refusal witnesses, malformed approval binding, version gap, version regression, reordering, illegal transitions (approval onto DRAFT, submission after approval, events after terminal SUPERSEDED and terminal REJECTED), binding drift (budget hash, content hash, goal ref, expectedGoalVersion vs its own witness, approval binding not over this content), epoch drift (initial epoch != 1, successor skipping the predecessor epoch, malformed predecessor epoch), and a malformed supersession authority hash.

IDENTITY SEMANTICS PINNED BOTH WAYS, which is the half a duplicate-only test always misses: byte-identical redelivery of the last event AND of the entire history end-to-end are accepted, leaving state and the event list equal to the reducer's; a redelivery at an already-applied version with one drifted byte, and one reusing a version under a different commandId, both refuse GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_IDENTITY_CONFLICT.

COMPOUND-APPROVAL TRAP COVERED (the architect's named risk): a dedicated test first asserts the precondition that makes the case load-bearing — the Approved and Activated events genuinely share one commandId at consecutive versions — then asserts replay treats them as distinct. Keying identity on commandId alone would collapse them; keying on (version, commandId) does not.

Also asserted: refusals expose exactly `{code, layer, ok}` and never a partial state or event list; accepted results are frozen; the caller's history array is neither mutated nor returned by reference.

Two defects in my own first draft, both caught and fixed before the run: a malformed `boundHashes` expectation built from spread-undefined keys, and a coverage loop that assigned a reducer RESULT into a state variable. Both would have been type errors or vacuous assertions.

implementationPlan.description: IMPLEMENT THE CORE-OWNED EVENT HYDRATOR. Add `graph-revision-replay.ts` with a closed `GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_CODES` vocabulary and `CORE_GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY` layer. Snapshot the entire hostile input once via the existing planning snapshot machinery; require a dense ordinary event array and exact per-kind data keys; detach/freeze all accepted data. Fold only the lifecycle/version relation already declared by `GRAPH_REVISION_TRANSITIONS`, reuse `validSubmission`, `validBinding`/`sameBinding`, `validActivation`, `validRefusal`, and `validGraphRevisionState`, and reconstruct every GraphRevisionState field from event facts. Track `(version, commandId)` identities: byte-identical repeated delivery is idempotently ignored, while same identity/different bytes is `GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_IDENTITY_CONFLICT`. Missing create, gaps, illegal ordering, binding/hash drift, and epoch/succession drift get distinct stable codes; never return partial state on failure. Keep the new production module <=250 physical lines and add its exact one-line LF `.js` bridge.

IMPLEMENTATION. `graph-revision-replay.ts` is exactly 250 physical lines, longest line 106. Whole input snapshotted ONCE via `snapshotData` before any discriminator read, so getters/proxies/cycles/symbols/exotic prototypes cannot observe or vary the decision; every later check reads only inert snapshot data, and accepted events are the detached snapshot copies, never the caller's objects. `REPLAY_TRANSITIONS` restates `GRAPH_REVISION_TRANSITIONS` over event kinds (Approved from PENDING_APPROVAL, Activated from APPROVED, Rejected from DRAFT/PENDING_APPROVAL/APPROVED, Superseded from ACTIVE, and REJECTED/SUPERSEDED terminal by having no entry). Compound approval materialises the intermediate APPROVED state replay-side; the final state still equals the reducer's, which the generated equivalence tests prove. Identity is keyed on VERSION, with byte-identical redelivery ignored and any other bytes at an applied version refusing IDENTITY_CONFLICT — commandId alone would collapse a compound approval's two events, which is the architect's named risk. Refusals return `{code, layer, ok}` only.

VALIDATOR REUSE IS REAL, NOT DECORATIVE. `applyCreated` builds the seed state and hands it to `validGraphRevisionState`, so the hex/ref/version/placement floors are the aggregate's own validator rather than a restatement — that is what answers the non-hex-hash and empty-revision cases. Submitted/Rejected/Approved delegate to `validSubmission`/`validRefusal`/`validBinding` + `bindingOf`; Activated delegates to `validActivation` + `sameBinding`. One deliberate exception, commented in the source: `validActivation` folds shape and epoch into a single boolean, so replay reads the epoch relation first (via the exported `validSuccessionBinding`) to keep EPOCH_DRIFT distinct from a shape fault. That is ~4 lines of attribution logic, not a second witness contract.

THREE THINGS THE PLAN'S MEASUREMENT MISSED, ALL FOUND BY RUNNING RATHER THAN READING:

1. `SupersessionDecision["successor"]` IS AN INTERSECTION, not the bare kernel binding. It is `SupersessionSuccessorBinding & { readonly lifecycle: "ACTIVE" }` (supersession-engine.ts:44), so the emitted event's successor carries SIX keys, not five. My `exact()` tuple omitted `lifecycle` and every SUPERSEDED path failed EVENT_INVALID — 6 red tests. Fixed by adding `lifecycle` to `SUCCESSOR_KEYS` and requiring it to equal "ACTIVE" (the successor is ACTIVE by construction; that is the atomic authority move). Reading the type alias was not enough — following it to the intersection was.

2. THE 250-LINE CEILING APPLIES TO TEST AND FIXTURE FILES IN THIS DIRECTORY, mechanically enforced. `planning/planning-source-size.test.ts` sweeps EVERY `*.ts` in planning/ with "no allowlist, no basename or suffix exception", and its own header says the fix belongs in the offending file, never in an exception. My single 493-line suite was a hard offender. FORCED SCOPE GROWTH, +2 test-tier files beyond the plan's declared newFiles: `graph-revision-replay-test-fixtures.ts` (169) holds the reducer-driven generators and assertion helpers, `graph-revision-replay.test.ts` (140) holds accepted paths/controls/idempotency/vocabulary, `graph-revision-replay-refusal.test.ts` (236) holds the 42-case refusal table. All four files now measure 250/140/236/169. The fixtures file follows the existing `graph-revision-test-fixtures.ts` convention, registers no suite, and correctly takes NO `.js` bridge — the audit does not report it missing, which confirms bridges are decided by reachability from `index.ts`, not by filename.

3. `REPLAY_TRANSITIONS[kind].includes(current.lifecycle)` FAILED TYPECHECK with TS2345 "not assignable to parameter of type 'never'": indexing a const-asserted record by a union of kinds yields a union of readonly tuples, and `includes` narrows its parameter to the intersection of the element types. Fixed with the same explicit annotation `reduceGraphRevision` already uses at graph-revision-reducer.ts:236 — `const allowed: readonly GraphRevisionLifecycle[] = ...`.

REFUSAL TABLE GREW TO 42 CASES. Four were added while implementing, specifically so no production branch is unexercised: a successor whose own lifecycle is not ACTIVE (EVENT_INVALID), a successor naming a predecessor revision or predecessor content that is not this revision's (BINDING_DRIFT x2), and a successor skipping predecessor epoch + 1 (EPOCH_DRIFT). The closed-vocabulary test asserts the published codes equal the exercised set exactly, so adding a code without reaching it now fails.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Rebuild graph lifecycle inside daemon: rejected by task rail and would drift from core. 2) Persist reducer state and trust it: rejected because corrupt self-consistent state could gain authority without replay. 3) Replay original commands: rejected because durable projection reads GraphRevisionEvent and StoredEvent does not expose original command bytes. 4) Convert events back into synthetic commands and call reduceGraphRevision: rejected because events intentionally omit command-only facts (notably full supersession input), so synthetic commands would invent authority. 5) Add event hydration beside the reducer using the same validators/transition vocabulary, with generated equivalence tests against the production reducer: selected. Exact duplicate identity is ignored; conflicting bytes refuse.

planningNotes.risks: Compound `graph.approve` emits Approved and Activated with the same commandId at consecutive versions, so duplicate identity cannot be keyed by commandId alone. Exact duplicate delivery must not mask a conflicting event at one version. Snapshot hostile input before any discriminator/key read. Activation must match the approved binding/content hash and distinguish initial graphEpoch=1 from successor predecessorEpoch+1. Superseded event does not contain the full original supersession request; replay may validate event/state monotonic facts but must not pretend to re-authorize the original decision. Root export keys are exact-set pinned. `graph-revision-reducer.ts` is 241 lines and must not be grown; all replay logic belongs in the new file.
